- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp declines or volatility spikes; adjust downward bias by 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots after price spikes (e.g., 40+), particularly in mid-to-late forecast horizon; cap forecast peaks at 5–10% above recent high.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast slope by 15–30% in next 3–7 days.
- Sentiment history flat (all 0.00) implies no market sentiment signal; if true outcome diverges sharply, assume model lacks event-driven adjustment; add 3–5% upward bias for 3–5 day horizon if no sentiment change.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often lag true trend by 2–4 days; shift forecast curve 1–2 days forward if recent 7-day trend is accelerating.
- Avoid overfitting to recent 18-day history; if forecast is too close to recent 3-day average, reduce forecast variance by 20–30% to prevent overconfidence in short-term noise.
